name: DS3218 20 kg digital servo (180°)
description: DSSERVO DS3218 high-torque digital metal-gear servo, 180° version: a 500-2500 µs pulse (1500 µs neutral, 3 µs dead band) at 50-330 Hz sets the angle 0-180°. Runs on 4.8-6.8 V; about 18 kg·cm and 1.8 A stall at 5 V (21.5 kg·cm, 2.6 A at 6.8 V), 4-5 mA idle; DSSERVO does not publish a running current, so about 0.9 A while moving under load is assumed for supply planning. Sold as: DSSERVO DS3218MG 20KG digital servo, 180° version (3-wire lead with a 2.54 mm female plug: white signal, red V+, black GND), also sold under DIYmall and other resellers' names.
eli5: A strong little motor that turns its arm to whatever angle your board asks for, from 0 to 180 degrees.

pins.name: SIG
pins.description: Signal (white wire): 50 Hz PWM, 500-2500 µs pulse = 0-180°; 3.3 V logic works

pins.name: V+
pins.description: Motor supply (red wire), 4.8-6.8 V; needs up to 1.8 A at stall, so use a separate 5-6 V supply for anything beyond light loads

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground (black wire); must be shared with the microcontroller ground

buildNotes: Order is signal, V+, GND on the 3-pin plug: white = signal, red = V+, black = ground. Check the colours on your lead before powering it; a reversed supply can destroy the servo.

Do not power it from the 3.3 V pin. It needs 4.8-6.8 V and draws up to 1.8 A when stalled (2.6 A at 6.8 V), more than a USB port or the board's 5 V pin can safely give; use a separate 5-6 V supply (e.g. 4xAA NiMH or a 5 V 3 A adapter) and join its ground to the board's ground.
Supply planning: about 0.9 A while moving under load (estimate; not published), 1.8 A stalled at 5 V. Turn the PWM off (duty 0) when the arm need not hold position to save power.
Drive SIG with 50 Hz PWM: 500 µs = 0°, 1500 µs = 90° (neutral), 2500 µs = 180°. The 270° version uses the same pulse range for 0-270°.
Put a 470-1000 µF capacitor across V+ and GND near the servo to stop the board resetting when the motor starts.

example.code:
from machine import Pin, PWM
import time

# DS3218 (180 deg version): 500 us = 0 deg, 1500 us = 90 deg, 2500 us = 180 deg, 50 Hz frame
servo = PWM(Pin({SIG}), freq=50)

def angle(deg):
    deg = max(0, min(180, deg))
    us = 500 + deg * 2000 / 180
    servo.duty_u16(int(us * 65535 / 20000))

while True:
    angle(30)
    print('angle 30')
    time.sleep(1.5)
    angle(120)
    print('angle 120')
    time.sleep(1.5)

library.note: Passed the Sparkbench part check in simulation and matched an independent datasheet reading. Not yet tested on real hardware.
